purpose: Whisper model-size benchmark for ASR (#135): audio to transcribe, plus AMI's human word-level transcript as the accuracy reference
split: Mix-Headset audio stream for the two meetings already in the real-data slice (ami.manifest.json); reference transcript from the manual annotations' words/ layer

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
license.summary: The AMI download page (https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/download/) states, verbatim: "All of the signals and transcription, and some of the annotations, have been released publicly under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Licence (CC BY 4.0)." The Mix-Headset audio is one of those signals, and the words/ layer is that transcription; both come from the same source page as the annotations in ami.manifest.json. CC BY 4.0 permits use (including commercial) and adaptation, requires attribution (credit the creators, link to the licence, indicate any changes), and is provided as-is with no warranty.

annotations.note: The same package (same sha256) as ami.manifest.json. Only its words/ layer is used here: one XML file per speaker (A-D), each word with a start time, so the four speakers interleave into one reference transcript by sorting on starttime.

package.note: Mix-Headset is a single channel mixed from all participants' headset microphones: the cleanest stream and one file per meeting instead of one per speaker. AMI publishes no checksums for the signals; the audio sha256 values in ami-audio.sha256 were computed on download. Put the audio in local-data/ami/audio/ and unzip the annotations to local-data/ami/ami_public_manual_1.6.2/. Everything under local-data/ is gitignored; this manifest + ami-audio.sha256 are the reproducible pointer.
